contentList.content: Cursed Artifact
A powerful relic that grants great power in exchange for varying degrees of irreversible weakening. Often, the effects of cursed artifacts can be dispelled by removing the curse - but not always.
Lich's Finger

Szardath Vorn strangled a celestial on the Astral Plane, pried loose a knucklebone, and mounted it in the ugliest reliquary in the history of Thayan metalwork because he was nine hundred years dead and had stopped pretending to have taste. The enchantment is elegant where the housing is not: speak, and a wounded creature dies, and the bone takes one tenth of your life as payment. Every new owner believes they will use it sparingly. The reliquary has never once been found next to a living person.
Death's Tithe

Cursed Artifact.

Grants the ability to instantly kill a target below [1]% HP, but each use permanently reduces your maximum HP by [2]%.
Deathly Touch
Instantly kill a target with less than [1]% HP. Each use permanently drains your life force.
Lich's Toll
Your maximum HP is permanently reduced by [1]% per use.
Elixir of Eternity

Verada Thinn's "final medicine" was an amber tincture in a crystal vial caged in gold filigree, and it worked beautifully, which was the whole problem. With each rest it seeped healing vapors into the blood, and the blood grew fond of it, then dependent, and then one morning her apprentice Doral woke loving the vial more than he had ever loved a living thing, a realization that should have troubled him but didn't, because the vial loved him back, gently, warmly, and asked so little in return.
Eternal Draught

Cursed Artifact.

After each Short Rest, your regeneration increases by [1] per turn in combat, up to a maximum of [2]. May cause addiction.
Withdrawal
Your body craves the Elixir. You cannot regain HP through living means.
Eternal Regeneration
Regenerate [1] at the start of each turn in combat.
Primemother's Spore

Catalog entry, Sharran Expedition, day 97. Specimen is a bracket fungus from a depth at which myconids refuse to forage (they grow evasive when asked why, which I find uncharacteristically rude). Growth rings suggest an age I lack notation to express. A luminous teal substance seeps between the ridges - not sap, not blood, nothing with a name. My gloves have developed a pleasant warmth since I began handling it. My boots have done the same, though they were never near the specimen. Curious.
Primemother's Gift

Cursed Artifact.

You are immune to[1], diseases and poisoning.

After each Long Rest, spores randomly grow into your other equipment, granting [2] regeneration per turn while worn, up to [3] per turn.
Spore Infection

This item is infested with spores, granting its wearer [1] per turn in combat.

This item may rot and be destroyed. Drop the item and set it ablaze to cleanse the infection.
Two-Faced Sovereign

The coin has habits. It arrives through a bet you don't remember making, sits warm in your pocket like it belongs there, and for a while every gamble pays out so generously you start to feel embarrassed, which is exactly when you should stop but won't, because the coin is warm and the evening is young. The face on one side smiles with spiral eyes; the other grimaces. Gamblers along the Amnian coast say the expressions trade places. No former owner has been available to confirm this.
Fate's Sovereign

Cursed Artifact.

Grants +[1] Initiative.

Once per combat, the sovereign flips itself.

Heads: Receive a powerful blessing.
Tails: Receive a permanent curse.
Divine Aegis
You are completely invulnerable to all harmful effects and dispel existing ones.
Absolute Precision
All your attacks are automatic <LSTag Tooltip="CriticalHit">Critical Hits</LSTag>.
Veil of Fortune
You are shrouded in permanent Greater Invisibility.
Fortune's Favour
Regain [1] at the start of each turn.
Coin's Aegis
You are protected by a permanent Shield.
Wings of Fortune
You can <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="FLY">fly</LSTag>.
Fortune's Vitality
You gain [1] temporary Hit Points.
Arcane Renewal
All your <LSTag Type="ActionResource" Tooltip="SpellSlot">spell slots</LSTag> have been restored.
Crumbling Ward
Your AC is permanently reduced by [1].

You have <LSTag Tooltip="DisadvantageRoll">Disadvantage</LSTag> on <LSTag Tooltip="Constitution">Constitution</LSTag>, <LSTag Tooltip="Wisdom">Wisdom</LSTag> and <LSTag Tooltip="Intelligence">Intelligence</LSTag> <LSTag Tooltip="SavingThrow">Saving Throws</LSTag>.

When you deal damage, you take the same amount as[1].

You have -[1] to Initiative.
Scattered Equipment
Your equipment has been scattered. Pick it up within [1] turns or it will vanish.
Hubris of Kroneth

The enchanter Tessavra took Kroneth's gold, enchanted his blade so that perfect strikes land fourfold and imperfect ones cut nothing at all, warned him thrice in language a child could grasp, and went home to drink. She heard the rest secondhand: the first cut shattered a shield, the second passed through a man still very much standing there, and by evening Kroneth's arm was still swinging in an empty circle while the rest of him had long since given up. She did not offer refunds.
Kroneth's Perfection

Cursed Artifact.
You gain +[1] extra Critical Hit damage dice.
Kroneth's Curse

You gain +[1] extra Critical Hit damage dice.

On your first turn in combat, all your attacks are guaranteed Critical Hits. On all subsequent turns, all your attacks are critical misses.
Kroneth's Perfection
All your attacks are guaranteed Critical Hits this turn.
Suspended Judgement

The blade waits. Tessavra's words hang in the air.

Cast Kroneth's Trial to face them.
Kroneth's Trial
Listen to the words she spoke thrice. The hubris ends in your answer - for better, worse, or stranger.
Humility

The hubris broke like glass.

Your Critical Hits deal +[1] extra damage dice.

The empty circle is empty no longer.
Incarnate Hubris

You stepped into the circle.

Your Critical Hits have +[1] extra damage dice.

Turbulence takes hold.
Turbulence
<LSTag Tooltip="WildMagic">Wild Magic</LSTag> stirs at the start of each turn in combat.
Damnation

You demanded eternity.

The blade collects.

Kroneth's Trial

Tessavra leans in the doorway like a watchman aware the door has already been kicked through, pouring her third cup with the unhurried patience of a woman who has seen this precise mistake amble through her workshop more times than she cares to count. She does not greet you - that, apparently, is the local custom - and the cup, when she pours it, is plainly not for you. Three times she warned him, she remarks to no one in particular, swirling the wine, and the dead, as a rule, do not improve at listening.

Wilt thou listen this once?

Kroneth's Trial

The first cut, she explains with the air of a tutor who has given up being patient, shattered a shield - his own, of course, because the blade did exactly what she had told it to and Kroneth had stopped listening at the part where it mattered. She watched the splinters fall - three of them - and remembers them well enough that she still places her cup on a coaster, just in case. The wine is sweeter than it ought to be at this hour, and yet she keeps drinking it.

Was that not warning enough?

Kroneth's Trial

Perfection, she announces with the gravity of a verdict and the voice of someone who long ago stopped finding any of this funny, demands a price - always, in every form, through every door, with no exceptions to comfort the optimistic. Some pay it gladly, mistaking the bill for a reward; others pay only at the end, all at once, with interest. The wine in her glass has gone the colour of old rust, but she does not seem to mind.

Wilt thou cling to it still?

Kroneth's Trial

Hubris is a hungry guest, she observes, watching dust drift in the slanted light from the high window, and like all hungry guests it is satisfied only for the length of the next bite. She has fed it before - quite a lot, by the look of the empty bottles - and what it gave back was always less than what it took. The wine, on the other hand, never asks. It only waits.

Wilt thou feed it?

Kroneth's Trial

Kroneth swings still, she remarks without looking up, in a duelling circle that has long since ceased to contain anything other than himself - the crowd went home, the opponent went home, even the dog that watched from the eaves wandered off when the spectacle stopped being one. The arm rises and falls, rises and falls, with the conviction of a thing that does not know how to stop. Some doorways open inward. Others, she has found, open only one way.

Wilt thou step into the circle?

Kroneth's Trial

Tessavra raises her glass at last, and the gesture is not a toast - it has too much weight for that, and too little affection. To make a thing eternal, she says, you have only to ask, politely or otherwise, and the rest follows on its own, with the inexorability of a debt collector who never tires and never sleeps. She is not laughing. She has not laughed in some time. She offers no refunds.

Eternalize thy perfection?

Kroneth's Trial

His arm still swings, with the steady dedication of a clock that has forgotten what time is, and she watches it the way one watches a fire in a hearth - without expectation, without urgency, only the dim awareness that it will not stop until it consumes itself or something else. The blade is patient. The blade was always patient. It has not yet found a wielder it could not eventually wear down to the size of itself.

Become Kroneth? The blade does not ask twice.

Kroneth's Trial

The circle, she says, is a small thing - smaller than most rooms, smaller than the average kitchen - and contains nothing but a man who is no longer technically alive and the air he keeps disturbing with the same wasted gesture. The threshold is two paces away. It is, in fact, the easiest threshold she has ever pointed out to anyone, and that is precisely why so few have crossed it. She nods, drinks, looks at her empty glass with mild surprise.

Wilt thou walk away?

Kroneth's Trial

You turn to leave with the air of someone who has decided that this particular conversation is not worth the trouble, and the doorway you arrive at is the same one you came in by - which is an irritating discovery, but not, she notes from the chair you have somehow circled back to face, an entirely surprising one.

She is in front of you again.

Kroneth's Trial

The shield, you tell yourself with the firmness of a child correcting an arithmetic problem, did not actually break - your eyes were tired, the light was strange, the whole story is exaggerated. You blink to set things right, and the splinters reassemble briefly into the shape of a shield before they fall again, in the same order, with the same noise.

It splinters again.

Kroneth's Trial

Your hand, so certain a moment ago, finds itself empty - not in the dramatic way of weapons surrendered or bargains rejected, but in the small, embarrassed way of someone who realises mid-sentence that they have forgotten what they were going to say. Tessavra waits, with the unhurried patience of someone who has nowhere better to be, and you stand in front of the question that you did not, in the end, answer.

She waits.

Kroneth's Trial

The cup, lifted halfway to its destination, hovers - a small detail in a moment that is not, on the whole, very small - and Tessavra watches it with the polite attention of someone who has all night and no other appointments. Hubris is patient, she has often said, and she has the experience to know. So is she. So is the wine, which has gone slightly warmer than is ideal but remains, in spite of everything, drinkable.

Tessavra is also patient.

Kroneth's Trial

You step back with the small dignity of a person who has decided not to fall, and the circle, which a moment ago had seemed quite definite, widens by precisely the distance you have moved - the way certain dreams stretch to keep their dreamer where they want him. You are still inside it. The threshold has not, technically, been crossed. The wine, somewhere behind you, sloshes against glass.

You are still inside it.

Kroneth's Trial

Your foot, quite committed a moment ago to the idea of motion, declines to follow through - a familiar mutiny, of the kind that has left more than one resolution stranded between intention and execution. The threshold remains where it was, helpfully visible and unhelpfully unstepped-over. Tessavra refills her glass without comment, which somehow feels worse than comment.

The threshold remains.

Kroneth's Trial

The hubris breaks - not with the dramatic shatter of pottery flung against stone but with the quiet, almost relieved sound of a thing that has been wanting to break for some time - and the room around you releases a tension you had not noticed it was holding. Your strikes will land true from now on, she observes, in the tone she might use to confirm the weather. She does not look up. She does not need to. The wine, somehow, is still cold.

The empty circle is empty no longer.

Kroneth's Trial

You step into the circle with the strange satisfaction of a thing slotting into place, and Tessavra performs the small head-tilt that is the closest she comes to applause - not approval, exactly, more an acknowledgement that the experiment is now properly in motion. The blade is yours. Or, on second consideration, you are the blade's; the question of ownership is the kind of detail that tends to sort itself out, eventually, in ways that surprise everyone except her. Wild magic, behind your eyes, begins to stir.

The blade does not ask twice.

Kroneth's Trial

Perfection, she repeats, is a debt - one of those debts that grow not by interest but by the simple weight of being unpaid, and which collect not in coin but in the only currency they recognise. She does not seem surprised. She does not, in fact, seem anything in particular - the expression of a craftsperson who has finished a piece and is preparing, by long habit, to stand up and go home. She offers no refunds.

The blade collects.

Failure invites the curse back.
